title: Urgent account verification messages
text: A notification claiming an account will be blocked unless the recipient immediately verifies their password may indicate credential phishing. Urgency is a warning sign, not proof by itself. Advise the user to open the official app directly or contact the organisation using independently verified contact details. Do not follow the message link or provide credentials.

title: Requests for OTPs or authentication codes
text: A message asking the recipient to share a one-time password, authentication code, recovery code, or login approval with another person is high risk. Do not share authentication codes with callers or message senders. If the request was unexpected, deny the sign-in request and check the account through its official app or website.

title: Unexpected payment and refund requests
text: A notification demanding an urgent payment, fee, refund, or transfer to unlock a service may be a scam, especially when it pressures the recipient to act secretly or bypass normal procedures. Verify the request through the official service independently. Never rely only on a phone number, payment address, or link included in the suspicious message.

title: Links in unexpected notifications
text: Treat unexpected links cautiously, especially when a message asks for login details, payment, identity documents, or app installation. Check the actual hostname carefully and beware of misspellings, misleading subdomains, URL shorteners, and unexpected redirects. A link's appearance alone cannot establish whether it is malicious; use a reputable URL reputation service when available.

title: Messages impersonating trusted organisations
text: Scammers may impersonate banks, delivery companies, government services, employers, friends, or technical support. A familiar logo, display name, or writing style is not proof of identity. Verify unusual requests using a previously known official contact method, and do not use contact details supplied only in the suspicious notification.

title: Unexpected APK or application installation requests
text: An unsolicited message asking the user to install an APK, disable device protections, grant accessibility access, or install a remote-control application is a serious warning sign. Do not install the file or grant the requested permissions. Verify the app through the official app store or the organisation's independently verified website.

title: Do not classify a message from one signal alone
text: Urgent wording, unusual grammar, a shortened URL, or an unfamiliar sender can be suspicious indicators but are not conclusive proof of fraud. Assess multiple signals together, check available reputation evidence, and communicate uncertainty. If there is insufficient evidence, classify the result as unknown or needs verification rather than declaring the message safe or malicious.

title: Minimise sensitive notification content
text: Notification analysis should minimise collection and transmission of personal data. Avoid sending one-time passwords, authentication tokens, full payment details, or unrelated private content to remote AI services. Provide clear user consent, allow app exclusions where practical, and retain only the information needed for the feature and its stated history settings.

title: Pressure, secrecy, and unusual requests
text: Messages that demand secrecy, threaten immediate consequences, promise an unexpected prize, or pressure the recipient to bypass normal checks may use social-engineering tactics. Pause before acting and verify the sender and request through a separate trusted channel. These patterns should raise scrutiny but should not alone determine the final risk rating.

title: Recommended actions for a suspicious notification
text: When a notification seems suspicious, do not tap its links, reply with personal information, send money, or install files. Open the relevant service independently, verify the request, and report the message through the service's official reporting channel when appropriate. If credentials were already shared, change them through the official service and review account security.
